title: Initial-state matching and stability diagnostics for a counter-streaming electron-fluid closure
abstract: This diagnostic comment examines initial-state controls in arXiv:2607.07106v1 using the published decks, archived PIC moments and reloaded initial fluid output. The central two-population moment identities are correct. However, the PIC input specifies proper momentum where the fluid input specifies ordinary velocity. The saved fluid states corroborate their initializers to roundoff. Relative to either fluid model, the initial PIC moment-current profile differs by $9.87\%$ in the full-domain, $x$-averaged relative $\ell^2$ norm; the two lower-sheet central cells differ by about $11.6\%$. Their Cartesian velocity-covariance pressures are about $20\%$ lower in $p_{xx}$ and $38.4\%$ lower in $p_{zz}$. A conditional public-loader calculation explains the finite-temperature drift reduction, while separating verified archived moments from an unverified custom diagnostic implementation. No native deposited-current file is identifiable in the complete posted PIC inventory. Separately, an auxiliary homogeneous longitudinal benchmark has a finite-isotropization fluid mode with growth $0.00952\omega_{pe}$ where its collisionless kinetic reference is Penrose-stable. This is not a sheet eigenanalysis or a refutation of the source’s application-specific instability claim. We also qualify the symmetry-plane density explanation and give a cancellation-conditioned relative heat-flux bound. No new reconnection run is claimed. A matched-state rerun is required to establish dynamical significance; the source’s later nonlinear conclusions are not disproved here.
